proof_obligations.name: source actor-priority eligibility
proof_obligations.statement: Define actor-level eligibility over simultaneously ready actor instances.

proof_obligations.name: priority-reversal discrimination
proof_obligations.statement: Prove that the base and reversed assignments produce different eligible actor sets.

proof_obligations.name: priority-erasure identity
proof_obligations.statement: Formalize that a priority-erasing translation maps source programs differing only in actor priority to the same target program or target scheduler state.

proof_obligations.name: priority-erasure impossibility
proof_obligations.statement: Prove that one identical target behavior cannot be trace-equivalent to both priority-reversed source behaviors when those source trace languages differ.

proof_obligations.name: compiled ordering preservation
proof_obligations.statement: Provide actor metadata, precedence constraints, microsteps, or another target mechanism preserving the source actor ordering.

proof_obligations.name: forward actor-selection correspondence
proof_obligations.statement: Every source actor-priority-eligible dispatch has a corresponding target-eligible dispatch.

proof_obligations.name: backward actor-selection reflection
proof_obligations.statement: Every target dispatch permitted by the encoding reflects a source actor-priority-eligible dispatch.

proof_obligations.decisive_for: target conclusion 1 in a restricted scope
proof_obligations.name: priority-inertness theorem
proof_obligations.statement: Characterize cases where actor priority may be erased safely, such as no simultaneous competition, ties, or an already forced causal order.

proof_obligations.name: multi-actor benchmark
proof_obligations.statement: Implement base, reversed, tied, and absent multi-actor variants and compare source and target actor-dispatch traces.
